question: Patients join an eczema trial during a bad flare. Over the next weeks, what usually happens to those given a dummy cream?
answer: Their skin improves noticeably. Eczema, pain and blood pressure fluctuate, and people enrol at a peak, so the next measurement tends to be better whatever is done. Morton and Torgerson warned that this regression to the mean makes useless treatments look good. A before photo taken on the worst day flatters any product.
move: Anything picked at its worst will usually look better next time.
ask: Which change did I credit to something I did, when it was just a bad stretch ending?
trap: Without real treatment, a bad flare should stay bad or worsen.
reference: Morton V, Torgerson DJ, Effect of regression to the mean on decision making in health care, BMJ, 2003
